items.question: What was the change in the Net cash provided by (used in) investing activities from 2017 to 2018?

previous_f3_program: observe(at("company.net_cash_provided_by_used_in_investing_activities", "2017"), -71, "million_currency", cell("Net cash provided by (used in) investing activities", "December 29, 2017"))
observe(at("company.net_cash_provided_by_used_in_investing_activities", "2018"), -114, "million_currency", cell("Net cash provided by (used in) investing activities", "December 28, 2018"))
query("difference", at("company.net_cash_provided_by_used_in_investing_activities", "2017"), at("company.net_cash_provided_by_used_in_investing_activities", "2018"))

paragraphs.text: The following table summarizes cash flow information for the periods presented:

Net cash provided by operating activities increased $224 million for fiscal 2019 as compared to fiscal 2018. The increase was primarily due to more favorable timing of working capital changes including higher advance payments from customers, $59 million received for the Greek arbitration award and lower payments for integration and restructuring costs. These activities were partially offset by higher tax payments, the timing of interest payments and $60 million of proceeds received from the termination of interest rate swaps in the prior year.

Net cash provided by operating activities increased $242 million for fiscal 2018 as compared to fiscal 2017. The increase was primarily due to lower payments for taxes, integration and restructuring costs and proceeds received from the termination of interest rate swaps. This was partially offset by $24 million of cash paid related to the 2016 acquisition of Lockheed Martin's Information Systems & Global Solutions business ("IS&GS Business").

Net cash provided by investing activities increased $179 million for fiscal 2019 as compared to fiscal 2018. The increase was primarily due to $178 million of proceeds received for the dispositions of our commercial cybersecurity and health staff augmentation businesses, $96 million of proceeds received for the sale of real estate properties and $81 million of cash paid in the prior year related to our 2016 acquisition. These activities were partially offset by $94 million of cash paid related to the acquisition of IMX, higher purchases of property, equipment and software and lower proceeds from promissory notes.

Net cash used in investing activities increased $43 million for fiscal 2018 as compared to fiscal 2017. The increase was primarily due to $81 million of cash paid related to the 2016 acquisition of the IS&GS Business, partially offset by $40 million of proceeds from the settlement of a promissory note.

Net cash used in financing activities increased $2 million for fiscal 2019 as compared to fiscal 2018. The increase was primarily due to the timing of debt payments and higher stock repurchases, partially offset by $23 million of cash paid related to a tax indemnification in the prior year and the timing of issuances of stock.

Net cash used in financing activities increased $278 million for fiscal 2018 as compared to fiscal 2017. The increase was primarily due to $250 million of stock repurchases under the ASR program, $167 million of open market stock repurchases and $23 million of cash paid related to a tax indemnification liability. This was partially offset by $150 million of lower debt payments and $14 million of proceeds received from a real estate financing transaction.

items.question: Oliver owns a laundry shop, and he charges $2 per kilo of laundry.  Two days ago, his shop washed a total of 5 kilos of laundries.  Yesterday, it washed five kilos of laundries more than the previous day. Today, it washed twice the number of kilos than yesterday.   How much did he earn for three days?

previous_f3_program: collection("oliver.laundry_shop.earnings.three_days", "daily_earnings", "oliver.laundry_shop", source("How much did he earn for three days?"))
observe(at("oliver.laundry_shop.charge_rate", "current"), 2, "currency_per_kilogram", source("he charges $2 per kilo of laundry"))
observe(at("oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_weight", "two_days_ago"), 5, "kilogram", source("Two days ago, his shop washed a total of 5 kilos of laundries"))

offset(at("oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_weight", "yesterday"), at("oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_weight", "two_days_ago"), 5, "kilogram", source("Yesterday, it washed five kilos of laundries more than the previous day"))
multiple(at("oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_weight", "today"), at("oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_weight", "yesterday"), 2, source("Today, it washed twice the number of kilos than yesterday"))

rate_relation("oliver.laundry_shop.earnings.three_days.two_days_ago", at("oliver.laundry_shop.charge_rate", "current"), at("oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_weight", "two_days_ago"), source("he charges $2 per kilo of laundry"))

rate_relation("oliver.laundry_shop.earnings.three_days.yesterday", at("oliver.laundry_shop.charge_rate", "current"), at("oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_weight", "yesterday"), source("he charges $2 per kilo of laundry"))

rate_relation("oliver.laundry_shop.earnings.three_days.today", at("oliver.laundry_shop.charge_rate", "current"), at("oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_weight", "today"), source("he charges $2 per kilo of laundry"))
query("sum", "oliver.laundry_shop.earnings.three_days", "three_days")

items.question: Kelly needs school supplies to teach her class for an art project. She has 8 students and they will need 3 pieces of construction paper each. In addition to the construction paper, she needs to buy 6 bottles of glue for everyone to share. After Kelly purchases these supplies, she dropped half of them down a storm drain. Class is about to start, but she manages to rush to the store and buy 5 more pieces of construction paper. How many supplies are left?

previous_f3_program: collection("kelly.supplies", "school_supply", "kelly", source("Kelly needs school supplies"))
observe(at("kelly.class.students.count", "current"), 8, "count", source("She has 8 students"))
observe(at("kelly.supplies.construction_paper.per_student.count", "current"), 3, "piece_per_student", source("they will need 3 pieces of construction paper each"))

product_relation(at("kelly.supplies.construction_paper.count", "initial"), at("kelly.class.students.count", "current"), at("kelly.supplies.construction_paper.per_student.count", "current"), source("She has 8 students and they will need 3 pieces of construction paper each"))
observe(at("kelly.supplies.glue_bottles.count", "initial"), 6, "count", source("she needs to buy 6 bottles of glue"))
remove("storm_drain_drop", "kelly", at("kelly.supplies.count", "current"), fraction(at("kelly.supplies.count", "current"), 1, 2), source("she dropped half of them down a storm drain"))
add("additional_paper_purchase", "kelly", at("kelly.supplies.construction_paper.count", "current"), 5, source("she manages to rush to the store and buy 5 more pieces of construction paper"))
query("remaining_count", "kelly.supplies", "current")

items.question: Hally and her friends organized a high school reunion. To cover the cost of a late-night party that they planned for at the reunion, each attendee had to pay $100. After the party, Hally and her friends realized that the total expenses were $500 less than the total contributions. If there were 50 people at the party, how much money was used to pay for the party expenses?

previous_f3_program: collection("party.attendees", "person", "late-night party", source("50 people at the party"))
observe(at("party.attendees.count", "current"), 50, "count", source("there were 50 people at the party"))
observe(at("party.contribution_per_attendee.amount", "current"), 100, "dollar", source("each attendee had to pay $100"))

product_relation(at("party.total_contributions.amount", "current"), at("party.attendees.count", "current"), at("party.contribution_per_attendee.amount", "current"), source("each attendee had to pay $100"))
offset(at("party.total_expenses.amount", "current"), at("party.total_contributions.amount", "current"), -500, "dollar", source("the total expenses were $500 less than the total contributions"))
query("value", at("party.total_expenses.amount", "current"))

items.question: Jeff had 300 pencils and donated 30% of them. Vicki had twice as many pencils as Jeff and donated 3/4 of his pencils. How many pencils are there remaining altogether?

previous_f3_program: collection("jeff_and_vicki.pencils", "pencil", "jeff and vicki", source("Jeff had 300 pencils and donated 30% of them. Vicki had twice as many pencils as Jeff"))
observe(at("jeff_and_vicki.pencils.jeff.count", "initial"), 300, "count", source("Jeff had 300 pencils"))

remove("jeff_donation", "jeff", at("jeff_and_vicki.pencils.jeff.count", "current"), fraction(at("jeff_and_vicki.pencils.jeff.count", "initial"), 30, 100), source("Jeff had 300 pencils and donated 30% of them"))
multiple(at("jeff_and_vicki.pencils.vicki.count", "initial"), at("jeff_and_vicki.pencils.jeff.count", "initial"), 2, source("Vicki had twice as many pencils as Jeff"))

remove("vicki_donation", "vicki", at("jeff_and_vicki.pencils.jeff.count", "current"), fraction(at("jeff_and_vicki.pencils.jeff.count", "current"), 3, 4), source("Vicki had twice as many pencils as Jeff and donated 3/4 of his pencils"))
query("remaining_count", "jeff_and_vicki.pencils", "current")
